name: mc_command
title: Run console command
description:
Runs a command as the server console and returns its feedback. An escape hatch with full console privileges for what no other tool covers: items, teleports, game rules, weather, time, scoreboards, datapacks, whitelists.

WHEN TO USE: only when no other tool fits. Prefer mc_build over /fill or /setblock: it is chunk-safe, tick-budgeted, journalled and reports what changed.
WHEN NOT TO USE: to place or read blocks (mc_build, mc_inspect, mc_survey), or to get around a limit mc_build rejected (split the build instead; a vanilla command only removes the safety checks). /locate is refused by default (also via execute ... run): it searches on the main thread and a long search can crash the server; to find a biome use tools/findsite.py from the Ashlar repo, which reads the region files offline. /save-all, /save-on and /save-off are refused by default too: they change saving for every loaded world, including worlds a plugin keeps unsaved on purpose (a save-all once broke a duel arena mid-match); read live blocks with mc_inspect, mc_survey saveAs or mc_export instead. allowLocate:true / allowSave:true run them anyway; use them only when truly needed.

PARAMETERS: `command` with or without a leading "/", or `commands` (up to 64, run in order in one call, e.g. one /item or /data per chest when furnishing; each reply keeps 3 feedback lines). When a plugin such as EssentialsX has taken over a vanilla command name (tp, kill, give, time...), the reply ends with a note naming the plugin; vanilla:true sends minecraft:<name> instead. The console is not a player: @s selects nothing and ~ is relative to the world spawn, so name the player or use absolute coordinates.

SIDE EFFECTS: unbounded; not checked against protected regions. The administrator can disable this tool. Feedback sent to the console sender is returned (at most 200 lines / 16 KB); asynchronous feedback and log-only output are not. A vanilla syntax error is returned as "Syntax error: ...".

command.description: Console command, e.g. "give Steve minecraft:diamond 1" or "weather clear".

commands.description: Several console commands run in order, each as `command` would. Not with command.

vanilla.description: Applies to every command. Run the vanilla command even when a plugin has taken over its name (sends minecraft:<name>). Default false.

allowLocate.description: Applies to every command. Run /locate even though a long search can freeze and crash the server. Only for a short search (a nearby structure). Default false.

allowSave.description: Applies to every command. Run /save-all, /save-on or /save-off even though they change saving for every world, including plugin-managed worlds kept unsaved on purpose. Default false.
